title: Recording every transformation: reproducibility and auditing

videos.script: Sixteen lessons of decisions. Placeholders blanked, centuries chosen, typed totals recomputed, duplicate customers merged. {{decisions}} Each one was right. And each one is worthless if nobody can see it was made. {{worthless}} This lesson turns the course into something that can be checked. {{checked}} The raw files stay exactly as they arrived, and a fingerprint proves it. {{raw}} One command rebuilds every clean table from them, in order, and says what it did. {{run}} Every value it changed is written down, with the rule that changed it. Five hundred and eighty-nine of them. {{changes}} The promises the tables make are written as checks, and a broken table fails them. {{checks}} Run it twice and the output is identical, byte for byte. {{rerun}} And all of it goes under version control, except the data itself. {{git}} That is what reproducible means: somebody else, next month, gets your answer from your files, and can see every step on the way. {{end}}
